title: `idempotentHint`
description: Marks repeated calls as safe: calling twice has no additional effect.
question: Is the idempotentHint annotation present at each capture boundary?
usage_note: Not published. Candidate source: count of public MCP servers using this capability. Not estimated, so the panel stays empty until the corpus is scanned.
why: Retry logic that reads the tool definition at the capture boundary can only key on idempotency if the hint survives to that point. Where it is dropped, a retry has to guess whether repeating the call is safe.

notes.crewai: CrewAI: the adapted tool object exposes no annotations field, so the value is not recoverable after adaptation.
notes.genkit_js: Genkit (JS) 1.42.0: `createDynamicTool` builds the Genkit tool from the MCP tool's `name` (prefixed `<server>/`), `description` and `inputSchema` only, with `outputSchema: z.any()` and `metadata: { mcp: { _meta } }`; `annotations.idempotentHint` is not carried anywhere on the `ToolDefinition` the model receives.
notes.langchain: LangChain: retained on `StructuredTool.metadata`, but absent from the OpenAI-compatible dictionary produced by `convert_to_openai_tool`.
notes.openai-agents: OpenAI Agents SDK: `FunctionTool` keeps `_mcp_title` only. The behavioural hints are not carried.
notes.pydantic-ai: Pydantic AI: retained in `ToolDefinition.metadata['annotations']`. Not part of `parameters_json_schema`.
notes.mastra: Mastra 2.2.0: retained on the tool action's `mcp.annotations`; not part of the id, description or inputSchema the agent is handed.
notes.google_adk: Google ADK 2.11.0: retained on `McpTool.raw_mcp_tool.annotations`; the `FunctionDeclaration` in the model's `LlmRequest` has no annotations field.
notes.vercel_ai: Vercel AI SDK (@ai-sdk/mcp 2.0.73): toolsFromDefinitions copies the server's idempotentHint onto the tool's app-side `metadata.annotations`, not into the description or inputSchema a provider adapter serializes. An app can read it; the model is not shown it.
notes.ms_agent_framework: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.21.0: `load_tools` builds each `FunctionTool` from the MCP tool's name, description and inputSchema only. The annotations are neither in the function spec nor kept anywhere on the `FunctionTool`.
notes.autogen: AutoGen 0.7.5: `McpWorkbench.list_tools` discards the MCP tool after building the `ToolSchema`, so the hint is neither in the definition nor retained elsewhere.
notes.openai_agents_js: OpenAI Agents SDK (JS) 0.20.0: `mcpToFunctionTool` builds the `FunctionTool` from the MCP tool's name, description and inputSchema only. The `idempotentHint` annotation is not on the tool the model is handed and is not kept anywhere beside it.
notes.semantic_kernel: Semantic Kernel 1.45.0: `MCPPluginBase.load_tools` reads name, description and inputSchema only. No annotation is kept on the KernelFunction or sent to the model.
notes.llamaindex: LlamaIndex (llama-index-tools-mcp 0.6.0): `FunctionTool` keeps only name, description and the rebuilt `fn_schema`; the MCP tool's annotations are not kept anywhere on it, so the value is not recoverable after adaptation.
notes.google_adk_js: Google ADK (TypeScript) 2.2.1: `MCPTool` builds its `FunctionDeclaration` from name, description and the converted schemas only. The annotations are kept only on the TypeScript-private `mcpTool` field, which nothing on the model path reads.
notes.agno: Agno 3.1.2: `MCPTools.build_tools` registers each tool as `Function(name, description, parameters=inputSchema)`; the tool's annotations, title, icons and `outputSchema` are not carried, so `idempotentHint` reaches neither the model nor the agent.
notes.haystack: Haystack (mcp-haystack 1.5.2): `MCPToolset` builds each `haystack.tools.Tool` from the tool's name, description and `inputSchema` only, so `annotations.idempotentHint` does not reach the tool definition.
notes.smolagents: smolagents 1.26.0 (mcpadapt 0.1.20): mcpadapt builds each `MCPAdaptTool` from the name, description and `inputSchema` properties only, so the MCP tool's annotations are not kept anywhere on it and the value is not recoverable after adaptation.
notes.dspy: DSPy 3.4.0: `Tool.from_mcp_tool` builds a `dspy.Tool` from the MCP tool's name, description and `inputSchema` properties only; the tool's annotations, title, icons and `outputSchema` are on no `Tool` field and in no dict the LM is handed, so `idempotentHint` is lost.
notes.langchain_js: LangChain.js (@langchain/mcp-adapters 2.0.1): `MCPAdapter.listTools` keeps the server's annotations on the tool's app-side `metadata.annotations`, but the function tool `convertToOpenAITool` builds for the provider carries name, description and parameters only, so the model never sees `idempotentHint`.
notes.spring_ai: Spring AI 2.0.1: `SyncMcpToolCallbackProvider` builds a `ToolDefinition`, which holds only a name, a description and the input schema, so `idempotentHint` is dropped.
notes.beeai: BeeAI Framework 0.1.85: `MCPTool` exposes the tool's name, description and input schema. The MCP `Tool` it wraps is kept only on the private `MCPTool._tool`, so the hint is in no public field and not in the function dict LiteLLM is handed.
notes.copilot_sdk: GitHub Copilot SDK 1.0.19 (Copilot runtime 1.0.95): the provider tool carries name, description and parameters only, and the runtime's permission request names title and `readOnly`. `idempotentHint` is not kept anywhere.
notes.crewai-native: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): `MCPToolResolver` builds each `MCPNativeTool` from the sanitized name, the description and an `args_schema` generated from `inputSchema`, so the MCP tool's annotations are not kept anywhere on it and the value is not recoverable after adaptation.
notes.google_adk_java: Google ADK (Java) 1.11.0: `AbstractMcpTool.declaration` builds the `FunctionDeclaration` from the MCP tool's name, description, `inputSchema` and `outputSchema` only. `McpTool` keeps the MCP annotations beside it, through its public `annotations()`, so `idempotentHint` is retained in framework metadata but never reaches the model.
notes.langchain4j: LangChain4j 1.22.0-beta32: MCP tool annotations reach `ToolSpecification.metadata()` only; the `ToolSpecification` AiServices hands the `ChatModel` carries name, description and parameters, so the model never sees `idempotentHint`.
notes.koog: Koog 1.3.0-beta: `idempotentHint` is dropped. `DefaultMcpToolDescriptorParser` builds a `ToolDescriptor` (name, description, parameters) and `McpTool` keeps only the `Client`, that descriptor and a string metadata map, so `annotations` never reach the chat-completions request and are not kept anywhere in Koog. `McpToolRegistryProvider.fromClient` leaves `deliver_payload` out of the registry (`DefaultMcpToolDescriptorParser.parse` throws on its typeless `oneOf` and `fromClient` only logs it), so its hint is lost with the whole tool.
notes.google_adk_go: Google ADK (Go) 2.5.0 (go-sdk 1.8.0): `convertTool` builds the `FunctionDeclaration` from the tool's name, description, `inputSchema` and `outputSchema` only, and `mcpTool` keeps no other field of the `*mcp.Tool`, so `annotations.idempotentHint` is gone after listing.
notes.ms_agent_framework_dotnet: Microsoft Agent Framework (.NET) 1.24.0 (ModelContextProtocol 2.2.0): `McpClientTool` passes the model only the MCP tool's name, description, `inputSchema` (as `JsonSchema`) and `outputSchema` (as `ReturnJsonSchema`). It keeps the MCP `Tool` it was built from as the public `ProtocolTool` property, so `idempotentHint` is retained in framework metadata but never reaches the model.

summary: A framework can keep the annotation outside the captured definition, in its own tool metadata, where an application policy layer can still read it. That counts as retained elsewhere.
